problem: Given the linear transformation $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-z \\ x-y+z \\ 3z-6x\end{aligned}],$ find $\text{nullity}(T).$
worked_solution:
First, we write down the standard matrix of $T:$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -6 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Recall that $\text{nullity}(T)=\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)).$

In order to find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T)),$ we reduce $T$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}T & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -6 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & \frac{3}{2} \\ -6 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & -1 & \frac{3}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has $1$ non-pivot column (the $3$rd one). Therefore, 

$$
\text{nullity}(T)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(T))=1.
$$
